title: Erdős Problem #740: Chromatic Number and Odd Cycle Avoidance
description: Must every graph with infinite chromatic number 𝔪 contain a subgraph with χ = 𝔪 that avoids all odd cycles of length ≤ r?

meta.author: Erdős-Hajnal (conjecture), Rödl (partial result)
meta.assumptions: 2 axiom(s) and 1 sorry(s). See the Lean source for details.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Hajnal posed this problem about preserving chromatic number while avoiding short odd cycles. It first appeared in Erdős's 1981 paper 'On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved' ([Er81]), where he listed it among approximately 50 problems he considered most important in combinatorics. Rödl proved the case 𝔪 = ℵ₀ and r = 3 (triangle-free) in 1977, using a sophisticated probabilistic argument involving random vertex selection. The problem also appears in Erdős's 1995 survey [Er95d] on combinatorial set theory. The general case and the threshold function f_r(𝔪) remain open, connecting infinite combinatorics, set theory, and structural graph theory. The problem sits at the intersection of Ramsey theory and chromatic graph theory, building on Erdős's seminal 1959 result that graphs with arbitrarily high girth and chromatic number exist.
overview.problemStatement: Let 𝔪 be an infinite cardinal and G be a graph with chromatic number 𝔪. Let r ≥ 1. Must G contain a subgraph of chromatic number 𝔪 which does not contain any odd cycle of length ≤ r?
overview.text: Must every graph with infinite chromatic number 𝔪 contain a subgraph with χ = 𝔪 that avoids all odd cycles of length ≤ r?
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize chromatic numbers for infinite graphs using Mathlib's Cardinal type, define cycles and odd cycle avoidance as Lean structures, and state the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture in full generality. Rödl's theorem for the countable triangle-free case is declared as an axiom. We prove that the girth variant (avoiding ALL short cycles) implies the odd cycle variant, and show the bipartite limitation: no bipartite subgraph can have χ > 2, so the parameter r must be finite. The formalization also addresses the threshold function question and finite analogs.
keyInsights: Rödl proved (1977): every ℵ₀-chromatic graph has a triangle-free subgraph with χ = ℵ₀, using probabilistic methods in infinite combinatorics
The general case for arbitrary infinite cardinals (ℵ₁, ℵ₂, ...) remains open, and may depend on set-theoretic axioms beyond ZFC
The threshold function f_r(𝔪) question asks for quantitative bounds: how much chromatic surplus is needed to guarantee the desired subgraph?
The girth variant (avoiding ALL cycles ≤ r) is strictly stronger than the odd cycle version, since it also forbids even short cycles
Bipartite graphs have χ ≤ 2, so eliminating ALL odd cycles (r = ∞) fails for 𝔪 > 2 — the parameter r must be finite
Erdős's 1959 probabilistic existence proof shows graphs with arbitrarily high girth and chromatic number exist, providing the backdrop for this conjecture
prerequisites: Graph theory fundamentals: chromatic number, proper colorings, and graph homomorphisms
Cycle structure in graphs: odd cycles, girth, and bipartiteness characterization
Infinite cardinal arithmetic and the cardinals aleph_0, aleph_1, etc.
Probabilistic method in combinatorics and Ramsey-theoretic arguments

sections.summary: States the main conjecture erdosHajnalConjecture for general infinite cardinals and r, plus the triangle-free specialization (r = 3) and the countable case (𝔪 = ℵ₀). This is the formal statement of Erdős Problem #740.

sections.title: Part V: Rödl's Theorem

sections.title: Part VI: The General Function f_r(𝔪)
sections.summary: Formalizes the threshold function question: does there exist a cardinal f such that χ(G) ≥ f guarantees the desired subgraph? Records that this quantitative refinement remains open for most parameters.

sections.summary: Defines girth, the stronger girthConjecture (avoiding ALL short cycles), and proves girth_implies_odd: the girth conjecture implies the odd cycle conjecture. This is one of the few fully verified results in the file.

sections.title: Part IX: Bipartite Subgraphs

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #740 asks whether graphs with infinite chromatic number 𝔪 must contain subgraphs preserving that chromatic number while avoiding short odd cycles. The formalization captures the full landscape: Rödl's 1977 theorem resolving the countable triangle-free case (𝔪 = ℵ₀, r = 3), the stronger girth variant and its implication of the odd cycle version, the bipartite impossibility for 𝔪 > 2, and the open threshold function question.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: The problem lies at the intersection of infinite combinatorics, cardinal arithmetic, and structural graph theory. A positive resolution for all infinite cardinals would establish a deep connection between chromatic number and cycle structure in infinite graphs.

The threshold function question connects to quantitative Ramsey theory. The problem may also interact with set-theoretic independence phenomena, as results about uncountable cardinals sometimes depend on axioms beyond ZFC.
openQuestions: Does the conjecture hold for all infinite cardinals 𝔪 (particularly uncountable cardinals like ℵ₁)?
Can Rödl's result be extended to r > 3 for countable chromatic number?
Does the threshold function f_r(𝔪) exist, and if so, what are its growth rates?
Is the answer for uncountable cardinals independent of ZFC (does it depend on set-theoretic axioms like GCH or large cardinal axioms)?
